research_seed.discovery_query: boarding stable Lexington Kentucky official website

source_candidates.evidence_excerpt: Contact section: 4630 Bosworth Ln, Lexington, KY 40510. Email: keeneridgefarm@gmail.com. Contact form available. Operating hours listed (Mon-Fri).

About Us: Keene Ridge Farm is nestled in the heart of Central Kentucky on 170 rolling acres near Keeneland off Bosworth Rd. Owner Ann Bakhaus transitioned from thoroughbred breeding to a full boarding farm. Multiple barns (Barn A, B, C), 75'x100' indoor arena, 100'x200' outdoor arena, covered round pen, lunging ring, over 20 large fields and paddocks. Full board $775, pasture board $450, mare retirement $450. Services: boarding, retirement, horseback riding lessons, workshops/clinics.

Mission Statement: 'Our Mission at Keene Ridge Farm is to give the highest quality care to our horses.' Boarding options published with full pricing details. Multiple barns with 12'x12' stalls. 'We schedule routine blacksmith and vet when needed.' Testimonials from boarders since 2020.

classification_decision.rationale: Keene Ridge Farm is a professional boarding and retirement facility on 170 acres in Lexington, KY. Owner Ann Bakhaus operates multiple barns (A, B, C) with full board at $775, pasture board at $450, and mare retirement at $450. The facility includes indoor/outdoor arenas, 20+ fields, and offers boarding, retirement, riding lessons and clinics. Blacksmith and vet services are scheduled routinely. The operation serves multiple horses clearly exceeding 3 head, across multiple disciplines and breeds (Thoroughbreds, Shires, Paints, Warmbloods, etc.). The official website self-presents as the farm's own site with owner name, full address, contact email, detailed pricing and services, and boarder testimonials.

criteria.notes: Professional boarding and retirement facility on 170 acres with multiple barns. Owner Ann Bakhaus operates full-time with published pricing ($775 full board, $450 pasture board). Mission statement: 'give the highest quality care to our horses.' Services: boarding, retirement, riding lessons, workshops/clinics.

Horse count not explicitly published. However, facility has multiple barns (A, B, C), 20+ fields and paddocks, boarders since 2020, multiple breeds housed. Strong commercial signals clearly indicate >3 horses but the exact count is not stated on the website. This will trigger the threshold exception review pathway.

The farm schedules routine blacksmith and vet when needed. As the boarding facility operator, Ann Bakhaus influences which farrier and hoof-care services are used for boarder horses. The boarding agreement states: 'We schedule routine blacksmith and vet when needed. (If you use anyone other than the farm blacksmith or vet, you must schedule them yourself and be there to meet them).'

criteria.criterion_label: Regular need for hoof-care products or services
criteria.notes: Professional boarding operation with routine blacksmith scheduling, hoof trimming included in mare retirement 'Spa Day' service. Regular need for horseshoes, nails, and hoof-care products for multiple horses across multiple disciplines.

Facility has jumps in both indoor and outdoor arenas, offers riding lessons, serves multiple disciplines. Boarders include hunters, jumpers, dressage riders. Breeds include Thoroughbreds, Warmbloods, Oldenburgs — sport and performance horse disciplines.
Farm was originally a Thoroughbred breeding operation but transitioned to a full boarding farm. No evidence of current breeding activity.
Works with professional farriers (farm blacksmith), veterinarians, riding instructors, and hosts workshops/clinics. Serves riders of all ages, levels, and disciplines.
Located in Lexington, Kentucky — the heart of Central Kentucky's horse country, near Keeneland racecourse. One of the highest equine-activity regions in the United States.
No recent buying, expansion, or acquisition signals found on the website beyond continued operation. The farm appears established rather than recently expanded.
